title: t says /t/
parentNote: Today is /t/, and it is the first sound your child has met that cannot be held — it is a tap of the tongue and then it is gone. The usual wobble is adding a little grunt on the end, "tuh", which turns "mat" into "ma-tuh" and stops the word sounding like a word. Clip it as short as you can when you say it yourself; children copy the version they hear. With /t/ there are suddenly real things to read: sat, mat, at.

activities.mouthCue: Tongue taps just behind your top teeth and lets go. /t/ — quick, no grunt after it.
activities.prompt: This one is over in a flash. It says…
Which one is the quick tap?
All three are quick taps. Find /t/.
Hold the first sound, then tap the second. Aaa-t.
Three sounds. Stretch the first two and tap the last.
Now the tap goes first. Watch where it lands.
Four sounds — the tall pole on a boat. Take it slowly.
Listen to the very first sound.
Now listen to the last sound instead.
Two of these have the same three sounds. Which way round is it?
Last hunt. Where is the tap?
